searchText: i think we are stuck on devnet5, there's no node serving slot 12670–23232 blocks. It's not clear to me what happened to the full nodes but prysm nodes cant sync to head without the blocks it kinda looked like network split again in https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1513089592172216362 we were able to do a checkpoint sync I think we should be a lil more strategic with future devnets. now that we have more mature Gloas impls I think we should gate participation on passing spec tests. And we should also in general give ourselves more time between spec release and devnet launch so that we have more time to work on passing spec tests. Feels like the last few devnets we’ve been kinda scrambling. Trying to think of what we could have done better to catch things earlier and make these devnets feel a lil more productive probably depends largely on the root cause... I just think launching a devnet 48 hours after spec release is a bit aggressive. And not many people around to debug on weekends also makes it tough. If we launch on a Monday for example we have more people online throughout the week to catch things as they happen On our end we’re brainstorming ideas to integrate panda cli into our devops flow to catch potential issues in real time so that we can more quickly respond i get what you're saying, just that if its an untested consensus issue it wouldnt have helped at all having spec test gates etc etc, just making the gates higher but not for the right reasons, so its probably worth understanding what happened before deciding what to do about the breakage etc. I do agree 2 days after a spec release is aggressive, and clearly only had a subset of clients etc. but we want to be careful about making 'rules' if we don't even know if it would have helped prevent the issue. yeah not trying to to create new rules, just feel like the strategy of spinning up devnets as soon as possible can actually hurt productivity sometimes would ppl be up to do a quick turnaround relaunch today? > Everyone said I was daft to build a castle on a swamp, but I built in all the same, just to show them. It sank into the swamp. So I built a second one. That sank into the swamp. So I built a third. That burned down, fell over, then sank into the swamp. But the fourth one stayed up. And that's what you're going to get, Lad, the strongest castle in all of England. Do we know what went wrong? these devents keep collapsing without clear root causes I'm sus of this flag:` export MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS=256` Could everyone confirm that its configurable on your node? We set this flag so that our nodes wouldn't store 18d worth of random blob data, but this might cause DA issues on nodes that don't take this value into consideration This is a flag that we have used before on blob devnet, but we only have lh and prysm on those Nimbus appears to respect it as a runtime config. All the references are to `cfg.MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS` where `cfg` is Nimbus's `RuntimeConfig` type we gonna do a quick relaunch with as many default mainnet variables as possible. And limit our blob throughput to about 3-5 blobs per block. Is everyone ok to yeet devnet 5 right now and in favor of a relaunch ? just pushed a new snapshot of `unstable` to `glamsterdam-devnet-5`, might as well test the current thing (I generally stop pushing updates to preserve things more when the devnets melt down), doesn't address anything specific to this devnet vs what was there before, but why not in teku is configurable and we should respect that. 4096 is not hardcoded. teku bugs ethrex error logs grandine bug <@&1417820113981145228> could you guys pls chime in and let me know what you think of this? Do we wanna spend some more hours trying to figure out what happened on devnet 5? OR we should relaunch? can we try to finalize it and let everyone checkpoint sync to head? can clients now sync to unfinalized roots? we can do that, I think there is a bug in lodestar I wanna get in first, then I can force them on Nimbus branch again which I think is the right one which head would you like to sync to tho? well we can pick the `lodestar-erigon-1` it seems to be still happily building blocks, but I rather go with nimbus/teku branch we seem to have 1 healthy node on each fork well it's down to 6 forks now, we had up to 13 over the weekend we should take fork choice dumps and figure out fi those are split because of fc, or because they didn't even see the other forks down to 4 forks gloas range sync

excerpts.author: 0xunclebill
excerpts.content:
I think we should be a lil more strategic with future devnets. now that we have more mature Gloas impls I think we should gate participation on passing spec tests. And we should also in general give ourselves more time between spec release and devnet launch so that we have more time to work on passing spec tests. 

Feels like the last few devnets we’ve been kinda scrambling. Trying to think of what we could have done better to catch things earlier and make these devnets feel a lil more productive

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: probably depends largely on the root cause...

excerpts.author: 0xunclebill
excerpts.content:
I just think launching a devnet 48 hours after spec release is a bit aggressive. And not many people around to debug on weekends also makes it tough. If we launch on a Monday for example we have more people online throughout the week to catch things as they happen

On our end we’re brainstorming ideas to integrate panda cli into our devops flow to catch potential issues in real time so that we can more quickly respond

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content:
i get what you're saying, just that if its an untested consensus issue it wouldnt have helped at all having spec test gates etc etc, just making the gates higher but not for the right reasons, so its probably worth understanding what happened before deciding what to do about the breakage etc.
I do agree 2 days after a spec release is aggressive, and clearly only had a subset of clients etc. but we want to be careful about making 'rules' if we don't even know if it would have helped prevent the issue.

excerpts.author: 0xunclebill
excerpts.content: yeah not trying to to create new rules, just feel like the strategy of spinning up devnets as soon as possible can actually hurt productivity sometimes

I'm sus of this flag:`    export MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS=256` 

Could everyone confirm that its configurable on your node? 

We set this flag so that our nodes wouldn't store 18d worth of random blob data, but this might cause DA issues on nodes that don't take this value into consideration 

This is a flag that we have used before on blob devnet, but we only have lh and prysm on those
